column3: NASB renders “a man, a master of a house” as “a landowner” and adds “early.”
NASB moves “And so they went,” which opens v. 5 in the Greek, to the end of this verse.
Close to the Greek; the opening words are in v. 4.
NASB follows the critical text: “standing around,” without “idle” and “hour” after “eleventh”; “idle” appears later.
NASB follows the critical text without “and whatever is right you will receive.”
NASB renders “as also to you” as “the same as to you.”
NASB has “Is it not lawful,” omitting the first “or.”
NASB follows the critical text without “for many are called, but few chosen.”
NASB follows the critical text with “will be raised up”; “flog” is rendered “scourge.”
NASB renders “say” as “command” and moves “in Your kingdom” to the front.
NASB follows the critical text, without the clause about the baptism; it omits “answering.”
NASB follows the critical text, without the baptism clause; it adds “it is for those.”
NASB renders the future “will be” as “is” in the first clause.
